subject: How BrightCart's fragmented prompt pattern maps to charges — rounding, minimums, and cache credits
messages:
From: Sophia Ruiz <sophia@brightcart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Billing for our fragmented prompt pattern — help?

Hi Logan,

We ran a two-week pilot and are seeing much higher token charges than we expected. Our integration sends thousands of short, single-turn calls that assemble a user session client-side (we call them 'fragments'). Example: 8–12 token user prompts + 20–40 token completions, repeated many times per session.

Questions:
- Are these billed per API call (i.e., each fragment rounded up independently), or does Redwood do any amortization across the higher-level session?
- How do rounding/minimums apply for tiny calls?
- Is there any discount/credit when the same prefix is reused across calls (we reuse a 40-token product-context prefix a lot)?

Can you share a clear worked example and a sample invoice line so we can reconcile? Attaching a short extract of the requests for reference (example-requests.log).

Thanks — this matters for our procurement conversation.

Best,
Sophia Ruiz
Head of Product Eng, BrightCart

Hi Sophia — thanks for the example log, that's helpful.

Short answer: billing is computed per request (input_tokens + output_tokens) and then normalized to invoice granularity, but we do have mitigations for high prefix reuse and for sustained streaming sessions. I've looped in Priya from Billing for exact math and sample invoice lines, and Sergio from Sales to pair on any commercial concession if the pattern is a material part of your production load.

We'll provide:
- a worked calculation for a single fragment and for an aggregated session;
- the exact rounding/quantum used for invoices;
- how prefix cache credits apply and the eligibility window;
- a recommended configuration (batching/prefix caching hints) to reduce your unit costs.

I'll follow up with the detailed breakdown shortly.

— Logan

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Ruiz <sophia@brightcart.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing for our fragmented prompt pattern — help? (detailed calc + examples)

Hi Sophia — Priya here (billing/product). Below is the explicit metering and invoice logic plus 3 worked examples from your sample: one tiny call, one typical fragment, and one aggregated session. I attached a calculator (billing-calculation-sheet.csv) and a mock invoice (sample-invoice.pdf).

Key rules (what actually hits the invoice):
1) Token measurement: we count input_tokens + output_tokens per API call.
2) Metering quantum (invoice granularity): we round each API call up to the nearest 16-token increment for line-item aggregation. That means a measured call of 34 tokens -> billed as 48 tokens (34 rounded up to 48).
3) Per-call minimum for discrete short calls: calls with measured tokens <= 48 are floored to 48 (this is the practical floor after applying the 16-token quantum).
4) Streaming/sustained sessions: if an open stream (server-side streaming) is active for more than 30 seconds, we switch to a session amortization where billing is aggregated every minute with a session-minute minimum of 256 tokens for that minute (helps high-throughput streams).
5) Prefix reuse (cache credit): identical prefix text submitted by the same customer within a 60-minute window qualifies for a prefix credit: the first occurrence is billed normally; subsequent occurrences within the window receive a 20% credit on the input_token portion of the metered amount (post-rounding). This applies only when we detect exact-match prefix tokens and KV-cache usage on the serving side.

Worked examples (from your attached extract):
A) Tiny single-turn ping
- measured: input 6 tokens + output 10 tokens = 16 tokens measured
- rounding: nearest 16 -> 16 (no rounding up)
- per-call minimum floor: 48 tokens -> billed = 48 tokens
- if price = $0.0008 / token -> charge = 48 * 0.0008 = $0.0384

B) Typical fragment in your log
- measured: input 40 tokens (includes 40-token product prefix) + output 28 tokens = 68 tokens measured
- rounding: 68 rounded up to nearest 16 -> 80 tokens billed
- prefix reuse credit: if this same 40-token prefix appeared earlier within 60 minutes and was cached, apply 20% credit to input_token portion (40 input tokens * 20% = 8 tokens credit applied as monetary offset after rounding).
- simplified billed tokens after credit (monetary offset): 80 tokens billed less (8 token equivalent credit) -> net billed tokens equivalent = 72 tokens (we apply credit as a dollar offset on the invoice line)
- charge (at $0.0008/token) = 72 * 0.0008 = $0.0576

C) Aggregated session (client builds session from fragments, 150 fragments over 10 minutes)
- measured total across session: 12,200 tokens (sum of measured tokens)
- per-call rounding applied to each call would normally increase the billed total modestly; however, because you used a sustained stream in some lanes we can amortize: where the same client kept an open stream >30s, we switched to session-minute billing for those minutes and applied the 256 token / minute floor. For minutes with heavy activity the floor is irrelevant; for sparse minutes it reduces the overcharge from many small calls.
- practical outcome in our calculation sheet: per-call billing (no stream) = ~13,000 billed-token-equivalent; with mixed streaming and prefix credits = ~11,400 billed-token-equivalent.

Notes / nuance:
- Credits are applied on the invoice as dollar offsets (we convert token-equivalent credit -> dollars using the same per-token rate).
- The 16-token quantum is for invoice aggregation only; internal real-time throttling still observes per-token usage for throttles/SLOs.
- We can set up a short pilot to enable more aggressive prefix-crediting for your account if you can confirm stable, deterministic prefixes (this requires a short instrumentation run so we can validate exact-match detection).

Action items I recommend:
- We (Redwood) run the attached billing-calculation-sheet against your full two-week extract to produce an itemized mock invoice (I can do this if you share the full request log).
- Tech recommendation: switch the hottest endpoints to a short-lived streaming path (30–90s) where appropriate and aggregate at the client for the remaining fragments — we can provide code samples to simplify this. That will reduce per-call rounding overhead.
- Commercial: Sergio, please see if BrightCart's expected steady-state load (after optimization) qualifies for a volume discount tranche in BR-9842.

I'll run your full extract once you send it, and then we'll propose a final numeric concession if the gap remains.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Billing & Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing for our fragmented prompt pattern — help? (next steps)

Sophia — quick summary and next steps so procurement has a path forward: 

Summary:
- Redwood meters per-request but rounds to a 16-token invoice quantum; very small calls hit a practical 48-token floor.
- Prefix reuse can yield a 20% input-token credit for exact-match prefixes within 60 minutes (applied as a dollar credit).
- For high-throughput lanes we can switch to minute-level amortization (256 tokens/min floor) which reduces rounding inflation.

Proposed next steps (pick one):
1) You send the full two-week request log -> Priya will return an itemized mock invoice and a line-by-line reconciliation (no PII required, just token counts and timestamps).
2) We schedule a 30-minute technical session where we show a short streaming snippet and a small client-side batching change that BrightCart can try; we can measure before/after savings on a small window.
3) If you'd like commercial help, Sergio can propose a short-term concession while you execute optimizations (we typically structure this as a one-month billing credit tied to verified prefix-reuse metrics).

Which would you prefer? If you confirm (1) we'll get the mock invoice back to you within 48 business hours after receiving the log.

Thanks — happy to coordinate times for the technical session.

— Logan
